name: Laxmi Dental Ltd
title: Laxmi Dental Ltd - 544339 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q4 FY26 revenue up 21.9% to Rs 74 cr with EBITDA margin 18.3%, but no capacity discipline signals; management refused numeric FY27 guidance and Bizdent pricing was traded for margin.

capex.quote: We have done a CAPEX of around Rs. 18.4 crores in FY '26.

summary.headline: Laxmi Dental Q4 FY26 revenue rose 21.9% YoY to Rs 74 crore with EBITDA margin at 18.3%, and FY26 revenue grew 16.2% to Rs 277.9 crore.
summary.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as a recovery quarter with highest-ever quarterly revenue of Rs 74 crore, up 21.9% YoY, and broad-based growth across dental lab, aligners and pediatric segments. EBITDA rose 41.8% YoY to Rs 13.5 crore and PAT reached Rs 10.1 crore, helped by a Rs 1.3 crore tax benefit tied to a labour code gratuity item. FY26 closed with revenue of Rs 277.9 crore, EBITDA of Rs 43.4 crore and PAT of Rs 28.9 crore, against a weak Q3. Management declined to give FY27 margin or growth guidance, and cited the company's Rs 99 crore cash balance and ongoing scanner deployment as strategic priorities.

financial_highlights.change: Minor sequential improvement; ~76% excluding scanner sales
vs Rs 4.3 crore in Q4 FY25; includes Rs 1.3 crore tax benefit
vs Rs 1.3 crore last year; company debt-free

financial_highlights.metric: Cash and bank balance incl. investments

segments.name: Dental lab (total)
segments.commentary: Record quarterly revenue of Rs 45.9 crore, up 27% YoY, with international lab up 40.9% YoY and domestic lab up 16.3% YoY to Rs 23.7 crore. Digital penetration in domestic lab is about 80%, with a medium-term target above 90%.

segments.name: Bizdent (domestic clear aligners)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 10.9% YoY in Q4 after a sequential recovery; management said margins were prioritised over pricing, which had been under pressure in prior quarters.

segments.name: Vedia (aligner raw material, mainly export)
segments.commentary: Revenue of Rs 7.3 crore, stable sequentially. Some March shipments slipped to April because freight costs roughly doubled, and in some cases nearly tripled, which delayed revenue recognition.

segments.name: Kids-e-Dental (pediatric)
segments.commentary: Quarterly revenue of Rs 5.4 crore. International registrations are in progress, with some regulatory steps cleared; no firm timeline given.

segments.name: Scanners
segments.commentary: Scanner sales were 211 units in Q4 FY26 and 1,009 units in FY26. Scanners carry lower margins and weighed on consolidated gross margin in Q4.

guidance_outlook: No numerical FY27 guidance. Management said it wants to do better than the 16.2% FY26 growth over the next two to three years, but did not endorse a 20% CAGR.

Management did not reaffirm the earlier target of 18-20% EBITDA margin, 75-80% gross margin and 13-15% PAT margin by FY27 or FY28. It said Q4 margins were in line with that range but would not give a timeline today.
Operating leverage is expected as people costs grow less than revenue; COGS will scale in proportion to sales. Automation and digital dentistry investments are planned.
Capex for FY27 will be set based on operational needs and revenue growth, funded from IPO proceeds still on hand.
US tariff is now about 10% (was about 50%). Management said this is not a deal breaker and expects US business to keep growing.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was about Rs 18.4 crore. FY27 capex will be balanced against operational capabilities and revenue growth, with no fixed amount given.
Scanner deployment remains a strategic priority: 211 units in Q4 FY26 and 1,009 units in FY26. Management wants to place as many as possible before scanners become commoditised.
Investment in automation and AI (AI Dent) continues to support cost structure and digital dentistry.
demand_pricing: Export share of revenue is about 33-34%. US is about 20% of revenue, and management said it is well diversified across customers, not dependent on Heartland Dental.
Management said the US tariff eased to about 10% from about 50%, and it absorbed higher tariff costs in the first half of Q4. It said the scale-up in the US was gradual and cautious.
Domestic aligner pricing was under pressure in prior quarters; management chose to protect margins, with Bizdent recovering in Q4.
Vedia orders were delayed by freight costs, but management said YoY growth is good and the business is not facing structural uncertainty.

The iScope 360 remote oral-health and aligner-monitoring product launched about two weeks before the call. It is sold through dentists at about Rs 2,000 retail with points-based subscription, and it may also be offered in export markets.
Competition is rising in domestic aligners and from funded players. Management said 22,000 dentists are active with Laxmi, against about 3 lakh dentists in India.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Bizdent revenue stay flat FY25 to FY26, and how much of the Q4 recovery came from pricing versus volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it chose to protect margins over price cuts during the pricing pressure. It did not split Q4 recovery between price and volume, and said it will keep balancing price against growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Vedia lower QoQ despite rupee depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight costs roughly doubled, and in some cases nearly tripled, which delayed March shipments into April. Management said YoY growth is good and there is no structural problem.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the lab business run rate of about Rs 40-45 crore per quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot give a number today, but expects growth in both domestic and international lab over the next two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for margins and growth for FY27 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give FY27 guidance. It said it wants to improve margins over the next two to three years and that Q3 was an exception. Q4 EBITDA margin was 18%.

qa_highlights.question: Is Heartland Dental's contract under review, and are more US DSOs coming?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there has been no change to the Heartland contract. It said more DSOs are being added but will not be announced individually, and that the business is diversified.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company considering acquisitions with its cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will evaluate opportunities that add value and will disclose them only once completed. It gave no specifics.

risks_watch: US tariff regime remains volatile. Current 10% rate could change, and the US is about 20% of revenue.
Freight costs and global shipping disruption caused Vedia export delays, which could recur at quarter-end.
Bizdent faces pricing pressure from domestic and funded competitors. Management is weighing margin against growth.
Gross margin is diluted by scanner sales, which carry lower margins. Scanner margin trajectory matters for consolidated margin.
Management has not reaffirmed the earlier margin targets. Watch whether FY27 margins hold at Q4 levels.
Kids-e-Dental international registration timing is uncertain.
Recent labour code changes affected Q3 gratuity and tax; Q4 PAT included a Rs 1.3 crore tax benefit that will not recur.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and long-term opportunity, but cautious on forward numbers. Management repeatedly declined to give FY27 margin or growth guidance and cited external micro factors and tariffs. It was evasive on Bizdent price versus volume and on the Heartland contract.
key_quotes: we close the year with a strong exit quarter, delivering highest ever quarterly numbers across key metrics.
Excluding scanner sales, our gross margin for core dental business remains stable at around 76% in Q4 FY '26.
I wish I could guide you at this point in time.
Scanner business is for us an enabler.

adds.what: Scanner deployment: 211 units in Q4 FY26, 1,009 units in FY26 (sales to dentists, not company-owned production capacity)
iScope 360 remote oral-health and aligner-monitoring product launched about two weeks before the call

growth.why: Management gave no numerical FY27 revenue or margin guidance, only saying it wants to beat FY26's 16.2% growth over two to three years; the only backing cited is operating leverage, automation and scanner deployment, with no specific capacity, orders or timelines, so guidance is vague.
